name: Black supremacy
summary: Black supremacy is a label for doctrines holding that black people are inherently superior to other races, best documented in the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad (to 1975), which taught that whites were a bred race of devils whose 6,000-year rule had ended. Its program was rejection of integration, a separate black state funded by the former slave-owning nation, black economic self-reliance, strict moral and gender discipline, and refusal of military service.
scope: Represents the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad (c. 1934-1975) as the best-documented black supremacist doctrine, with Malcolm X's 1963 statement of its program. Excludes the post-1975 mainstream Islam of W. Deen Mohammed, Black Hebrew Israelite groups, Nuwaubians, Rastafari and black nationalism that does not claim racial superiority, which differ in detail. Most answers outside race, separatism, religion and family are inferred and low confidence.

sources.usedFor: The Nation's own statement on separation, a separate state, self-defense, voting, intermarriage and economics.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nation of Islam teaching stresses self-help and black-run institutions, and says nothing on state health systems; adherents are split between wanting state redress and distrusting the white-run government.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The movement's economic emphasis was on black-owned businesses and jobs it created itself, not on wage law; no stated position, so adherents plausibly split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Elijah Muhammad promoted black capitalism through bakeries, groceries and farms, yet also demanded state-funded reparations; no doctrine on markets versus government in general.

public-ownership.rationale: The program centred on black-owned private and collective enterprise and on distrust of the white-controlled federal government, so white-state ownership of industry fits poorly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; the movement addressed racial rather than class redistribution, and Muhammad himself built an enterprise empire.

unions-good.rationale: The movement's focus was on racial self-reliance and black-owned jobs, with no documented stance on mostly white-led labor unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Nation bought land, farms and businesses and urged black people to own and control economic resources, implying respect for property, though it also demanded land from the state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement criticized white economic domination but proposed black enterprise rather than regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Nation preached self-reliance and criticized dependence on white society, but also demanded state support and reparations for black Americans, so the answer is split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective black-owned enterprise was encouraged, but no worker-ownership doctrine appears in the sources.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Nation was itself under heavy state surveillance and saw white-run government as hostile; inferred from that distrust of authorities.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Elijah Muhammad enforced strict bans on alcohol, drugs and pork among members, treating intoxicants as a tool of black degradation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The movement itself preached that whites are devils and saw white-state restrictions as hostile; inferred, with little direct statement.

strong-leader.rationale: Authority in the Nation rested on a single divine messenger, but the idea of a leader bypassing gridlock in a national government is not addressed.

state-harmful.rationale: The Nation demanded its own state and a separate territory, so it rejects statelessness even while condemning the existing white-run state.

limit-guns.rationale: Malcolm X for the Nation insisted black people have the right to defend themselves, and the Fruit of Islam served as a self-defense arm.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police are portrayed as successors to slave-era enforcers who traded bloodhounds for police dogs, and Muhammad told followers not to serve in the armed forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Nation required sexual abstinence before marriage and monogamy within it, so legal sex work conflicts with its moral code.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed; the program wanted a separate nation rather than a position on decentralization within the existing state.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Nation recruited from prisons and promised moral reform through discipline and its teachings; inferred from that conversion-focused work.

traditional-family.rationale: Muhammad's teaching prescribed patriarchal roles, male providers, female homemakers, monogamy and chastity before marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Heterosexual monogamy was required and gender roles strictly conservative; inferred as the Nation did not legislate on the point but its doctrine rules it out.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the pronatalist, conservative family doctrine and Muhammad's framing of black survival; no clear direct statement in the sources read.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Nation sought an Islam-based black nation and condemned Christianity as the white man's tool, so religion-informed public life is favored for its own faith, but a larger role for existing religion is not the aim.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Core demand: a separate state funded for 20 to 25 years by the former slave-owning nation, as redress for slavery.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Nation taught conservative, essentialist gender roles; inferred from these teachings.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Nation rejected white American culture and sought its own black national culture, so the statement splits depending on which nation is meant.

gradual-change.rationale: Malcolm X dismissed integration gains as tokenism and said white rule was scheduled to end, and Muhammad foresaw its imminent destruction.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No documented stance on immigration; the Nation's racial focus was on black Americans.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: the movement distrusted white-led Western institutions, though it also sought outside Muslim support; no direct statement.

free-trade.rationale: No stated position; the Nation stressed black-owned enterprise and economic self-sufficiency.

nation-first.rationale: The Nation put the interests of the black nation first and rejected integration; inferred, since the 'country' in question is ambiguous.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The Nation opposed black men serving in white America's wars; inferred opposition to American-led interventions.

open-borders.rationale: The Nation's program is separation of the races into distinct territories, the opposite of open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental questions never addressed; the Nation's eschatology is of destruction through divine action, not policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mixed: Yakub's story centres on a scientist, yet the Nation's expectation is divine intervention by the Mother Plane.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power never figures in the Nation's teaching; no basis for a position, so neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught that white rule would be ended by divine action and urged restraint, while Malcolm X asserted self-defense; adherents are split on human revolution.

central-planning.rationale: Muhammad built private and communal enterprises rather than planning; inferred, little direct evidence.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources record no view on worker or public ownership of firms in a market economy; the Nation's own enterprises were run under the movement.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design never appears in Nation teaching or Malcolm X's statements, so there is nothing to infer from.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Nothing in the sources on inheritance; the movement's wealth question was racial redress, not taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Never addressed; the demand was for a funded separate state, with emphasis on self-reliance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is never discussed in the sources; the economic emphasis was on black-owned local businesses.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's economic aims concerned black-owned institutions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Nation encouraged black ownership of land, shops and farms; inferred broad support for black owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Nation ran businesses, paid work and tithes; abolition of money is foreign to its program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are absent from the doctrine; no basis for either side.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages are not part of the Nation's program, which stressed self-help.

one-party-rule.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation was itself a religious body rather than a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred; the Nation's authority was a messenger of Allah, but hereditary rule of a state is not part of its program.

democracy-best.rationale: Muslims could register to vote and back chosen candidates, but integrationist democracy was viewed as tokenism and the Nation sought separation.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: no workers' council doctrine, and the movement was religious and racial rather than class-based.

right-to-secede.rationale: The central political demand was a separate territory for black Americans, a form of secession or partition.

natural-rulers.rationale: Doctrine holds black people the original divine race and whites an engineered race prone to violence and lying who were allowed 6,000 years of rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Malcolm X on behalf of the Nation asserted a right of self-defense, and the Fruit of Islam was a defense arm; Muhammad nonetheless held back from revolt.

war-builds-character.rationale: Muhammad told followers to refuse draft and military service in American wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: The goal was a separate nation under Islam, as Malcolm X described it, so state and religion are joined.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Nation sought a nation ordered by its own Islamic teachings, though its scripture was distinctive.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred; the Nation wanted a state of its own with its own defense force.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; Muhammad opposed black service in the US military, but a separate state's military was not detailed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The separate-state demand and rejection of integration aim at a nation made up of black people, with whites kept separate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: History is explained as racial: whites were created to rule for 6,000 years, not by class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed beyond the redress demand.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Never addressed; the Nation sought land for black Americans in the former slave states, not indigenous sovereignty.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents demanded reparations from the nation that held slaves; inferred sympathy for colonial reparations, though the Nation focused on America.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Africanism was rejected by Muhammad, though the Original Asiatic Nation concept spans non-European peoples; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation stressed collective racial uplift and discipline.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Nation imposed strict discipline and duty to the community on members; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The doctrine concerns race, God and history, and says nothing about nature's value apart from humans.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from the pronatalist, family-oriented stance and the notion of building a black nation.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Nation blames white rule, not industrialization, for black suffering, and itself built farms and businesses; no clear stance.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources show no stance on technological disruption; the Mother Plane expectation is prophecy, not policy.

human-enhancement.rationale: The Nation favored strict bodily discipline and diet; inferred. Yakub's eugenic breeding is cast as the origin of evil.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI governance is anachronistic for a movement of 1930 to 1975 and cannot be inferred from its principles.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic for the movement; its general distrust of state surveillance gives no firm answer.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Nation looked to a restored original black order, with white rule's 6,000 years ended; inferred from this return-to-origin framing.

direct-action.rationale: Muhammad urged separation and self-help instead of civil-rights marches and criticized King, but also confronted police at times; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources show no teaching that methods must mirror the desired society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement built farms, schools and businesses; foraging is foreign to it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gender-based role divisions were central doctrine, and enterprises were built.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is not part of the program, which emphasized work, discipline and enterprise.

production-for-use.rationale: The Nation ran profit-seeking bakeries and shops without a doctrine of production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Muhammad's analysis of exploitation was racial rather than class-based, and the Nation ran profit-making enterprises.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred; the movement is racial and religious rather than proletarian.

collective-farming.rationale: The Nation owned farmland, but whether it held collective farming as a principle is not stated.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; wars are attributed to the nature of whites in the Yakub account.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Nation demanded state funding for a black state, so a general rejection of taxation does not fit.

harm-principle.rationale: The Nation enforced strict personal moral discipline on members; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Nation treats the black nation as a collective whose redress and separation are demanded as a group.

conscription.rationale: Muhammad told followers not to register for the draft and served prison time himself for draft evasion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Separation, the right to leave integration behind, is the Nation's answer to its grievances, though the vote is not rejected outright.

state-as-business.rationale: No doctrine on running government like a business, though Muhammad was himself an enterprise builder.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed, though the call for state support to the separate nation points to material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; Muhammad's schools disputed with school boards, but no thesis about media power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Yakub account makes whites a bred race with an inherent violent and deceitful nature and blacks divine, a racial-hereditary claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is not in the sources; the Nation's own structure was religious.

total-state.rationale: Inferred; the movement ran its own institutions but did not advocate a totalist state.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Nation preaches awakening the 'dead' black nation from enslaved decadence to its original divine status.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Nation asked for a defined territory, not expansion abroad; Muhammad spoke of civilizing Africa.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Nation's structure demanded personal loyalty to its messenger, but the statement concerns feudal political order, which is not addressed.

bound-labor.rationale: The Nation's founding grievance is slavery and bondage, so any bound labor is rejected.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Nation taught that Christianity and white learning were instruments of white supremacy, and ran its own schools in response.

universal-morality.rationale: The Nation's morality is tied to race and revelation through its messenger, not universal reason.

single-common-good.rationale: No statement on a single reasoned common good; the Nation's concern was the racial interest of black people.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Muhammad ranked Orthodox Jews above most whites spiritually but taught that Jews were a Yakub-created race; inferred opposition, uncertain.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed beyond the Nation's own return to a black homeland.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation said slavery stripped black people of their language, which hints at sympathy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic votes in company management are absent from the Nation's economic teaching.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Nation ran its own schools, which clashed with city school boards, so support for choosing private schooling is inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

economic-freedom.rationale: Muhammad urged black enterprise, but no source links economic and political freedom as the statement does.

national-self-determination.rationale: The core demand is a separate state for black Americans governing themselves.

force-without-un.rationale: UN authorization of force is not addressed, and the Nation opposed black service in American wars.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Nation rests on revelation from Fard Muhammad and Elijah Muhammad as messenger, and faith claims such as the Mother Plane.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources do not address who should receive welfare or any split between citizens and immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Nation's self-help ethic stressed work and discipline; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; internal black business ties were encouraged.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation sought to restore a lost heritage, which cuts against.

dominated-front.rationale: Malcolm X and Muhammad framed black Americans and non-European peoples as one 'Original Asiatic' family against white rule, though Pan-Africanism was rejected.

workers-nation.rationale: Class organisation along national lines is not in the sources; the Nation organised by race.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Men are providers, women household keepers, a core feature of Nation teaching.

ban-interest.rationale: The Nation has an Islamic framing and Muslim-style rules, but a ban on interest was not located in the sources; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Nation demanded racial separation, though it asked this as a negotiated separate state rather than white-run Jim Crow, which it also condemned.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Nation sees the state as a white instrument of racial domination, not of class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not discussed in the sources, so no basis for an answer.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Nation rejected assimilation into white American culture.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed; the Nation's goal was a separate state, not reform of voting rules.

national-mission.rationale: Muhammad said the Nation's job was to civilize Africa and awaken black people; inferred sense of mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Nation endorsed male headship and does not treat it as an injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Black and white elites are called out, including 'Uncle Tom' leaders and the federal government that will not protect black people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Yakub's story involves eugenics, but state curbs on those with defects are not stated.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Nation criticized police as heirs of slave patrols; inferred support for accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Nation demanded a state-funded territory and spoke of an expansive moral order, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Members were to marry within the black community, and marrying whites was taboo; Malcolm X said only a man ashamed of himself marries out of his race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Nation teaches blacks divine and whites devils by nature, so equal moral worth is denied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Nation had no socialist doctrine, so the question of socialism in one country does not arise.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Nation saw the US as a white slave-holding state.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Nation sought its own Islamic order apart from the existing American legal order; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Nation was a proselytizing faith that sought converts from Christianity.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation had food rules on pork but not cattle.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Nation ran its own religious schools; the statement concerns state schools, on which it did not clearly stake out a view.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state theory is absent from Nation teaching.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The demand is for a separate state for people who do not consent to white rule; inferred from this.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

population-transfer.rationale: The Nation proposed voluntary separation with state funding, and not forced expulsion of a minority; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation's view is of racial struggle ordained by Allah, not progress by competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Nation was itself persecuted as subversive and was prosecuted for sedition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The framing of 6,000 years of rule over the black race as slavery fits a domination view, inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The sources show no teaching on constitutional checks; the Nation sought a state but left its design unspecified.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation was led by a religious messenger.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Nation recruited among the urban poor and prisoners, with programs of jobs and schools; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British policy question absent from the Nation's concerns; no basis to infer.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not addressed in the sources, and the movement did not focus on labor disputes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is blamed on slavery and white domination.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The program rests on the claim that integration cannot work and the races must live apart.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lot is nowhere in the sources; no inference possible.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Nation ran its own newspaper but the sources say nothing on government control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party commanding the army is not part of the Nation's teaching, which was a religious movement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed; the Nation's focus was black Americans, not immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of elected representatives is not mentioned in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Members were bound by strict discipline in the Nation, but party legislators are not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Nation sought its own sovereign state; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the armed forces is not addressed in the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Nation centred on a single messenger and ministers, and not bishops; not addressed as a political model.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rested on Elijah Muhammad as messenger of Allah, a religious leader at the head of the movement; inferred for a state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Muhammad's followers refused the draft and he was jailed for it; inferred applicability to rival-power wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Strict moral discipline over members' conduct; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not mentioned in the sources, so neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials does not appear in the sources on the movement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are not discussed, though the Nation did oppose black participation in US wars.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation encouraged ownership but no ban.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Nation supported self-defense and had the Fruit of Islam, yet no stated demand for an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Muhammad bought farmland and promoted agriculture for self-sufficiency; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Divided-nation reunification has no analogue in Nation teaching.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No documented view on university-educated people; the Nation did run its own schools.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Nation ranks races, with blacks divine and whites devils, and rejects equality of peoples.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources record no Nation position on capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Nation's sexual morality is strict and abstinence-based; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Nation has its own creation account with the Yakub story, but no stated position on public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Nation required chastity and modesty; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not addressed in the sources, though the movement defines the nation by race.

minority-language-support.rationale: Muhammad's teaching said slavery took black people's language, but no policy on minority language support is recorded.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Muhammad's followers refused the draft on religious grounds; inferred support for exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Nation enforced strict, uniform conduct among members.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign debts are not discussed; the movement's demand was reparations from America.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Nation said independence needs black economic self-sufficiency, as Malcolm X urged black economic leadership in their own community.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is absent from the sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The trade-off between freedom and development is not discussed in the sources.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Nation demanded funding for black Americans from the former slave-owning nation; aid to the world's poor is inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is not part of the Nation's teaching.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not say how a head of state should be chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Land-for-peace deals are not addressed; the Nation's own demand was for territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The sources give no view on the grounds of private property rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union's character is not a topic in the sources on the Nation.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation never appears in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; the Nation's Fruit of Islam defended its own members.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Nation judged policy by its doctrine of racial separation and prophecy, not by outcomes alone; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Nation's teaching holds that whites are devils to be destroyed by divine action and defends self-defense; absolute non-initiation is not its creed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The movement suffered sedition prosecutions and police clashes; inferred opposition to suspending protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Nation of Islam built its own religious institutions and schools under its own authority and rejected the white-run state; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Nation rejected the American political order and addressed no head-of-state question; neutral inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Nation's own program demanded a separate black state and rejected the US government's claim over black Americans; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Nation sought full separation, not autonomy inside the US, but would accept self-governing black institutions; split inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Nation honoured Elijah Muhammad as messenger, but taught no divine descent for rulers and rejected the existing order; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No stated position on tax structure; the economic emphasis was on black-owned business.

character-from-environment.rationale: Its racial doctrine holds that races have innate natures, with whites bred as devils in the Yakub myth, though it also stressed moral reform; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Nation demanded justice and strict moral discipline and criticised rulers who broke their own law; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: The Nation's teaching on space was mythic (the Mother Plane) and not about civilizational expansion; neutral inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No stated position on constitutional form.

leader-cult.rationale: Elijah Muhammad was highly revered within the movement, but public leader glorification in national life was not a stated aim; neutral inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: The Nation taught strict, differentiated gender roles with the father as head of the household; inferred from its family teaching.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Nation of Islam framed the conflict as racial, not class-based, and was no socialist movement; inferred from its race-first program.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from the demand for land for a separate black state and the Nation's own farmland purchases; it did not address breaking up estates as such.

refugee-return.rationale: The Nation sought separation, not return to former homes; no stated position, so inferred neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Its territorial demand was for land inside the United States, not a claim abroad; no stated position on claims beyond borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: the Nation disciplined its own members but as a minority did not seek state penalties for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Members' women dressed modestly under Nation discipline, but it never asked the law to require covering; adherents' view is inferred.

common-currency.rationale: The Nation said nothing on currency; inferred neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Elijah Muhammad taught a worldwide 'Asiatic' black nation and sought solidarity with Muslim and nonwhite peoples; inferred sympathy for cross-border unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a fully separate state rather than self-governing institutions inside the existing one.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Malcolm X stated that integration will not work and the Nation demanded a separate state rather than a fight for equal rights within white America.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Its history is a divine, race-based story (the Yakub myth) rather than an economic one; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: No stated position on cartels or competition law; inferred neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: No stated position on bailouts; the Nation stressed black self-reliance but said nothing on state rescues.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: As a persecuted minority it distrusted white majority rule but also demanded redress from the state; inferred mild lean against majority-only rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Nation taught strict, separate gender roles for men and women; inferred opposition to parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Nation urged black economic self-reliance within America, not a closed colonial trade bloc; inferred neutral on the literal claim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No stated position on trade agreements; inferred neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Nation relied on moral discipline, duty and communal sacrifice rather than state incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Malcolm X's 1963 statement limits force to self-defense, and the Nation refused military service; it did not seek to start a revolution by arms.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Its target was white privilege rather than inherited rank; no stated position on titles, so neutral.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Elijah Muhammad's schools and teaching centred black history and the Yakub account of race.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Nation taught that white rule was over and whites were devils, so rule over blacks by whites for their benefit is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Nation refused military service and sought separation from the United States, so national pride is not taught; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The program demanded separation and redress, not race-neutral rules; the sources do not discuss admissions or hiring preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: No source addresses money creation; the stress on self-reliance gives no clear direction.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: No source addresses capitalism's crises; the Nation backed black-owned business inside the system.

former-empire-influence.rationale: No source addresses it; the movement was concerned with the United States, not former empires.

delink-world-market.rationale: The program sought a separate black state and economic self-reliance, so economic separation fits; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Whites were seen as a ruling race, but the sources give no view on worker classes; inferred neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Nation opposed discrimination against blacks, though it also favoured separation; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The sources give no stated view; the Nation held that US law had not protected blacks.

missingStatements.text: Some races are inherently superior to others.
missingStatements.rationale: The central doctrine is that black people are the original, divine race and whites an engineered race of devils.

missingStatements.text: Black Americans should receive land and public funding for a separate state of their own.
missingStatements.rationale: The Muslim Program demanded a separate state funded for 20 to 25 years by the former slave-owning nation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific historical demand of the Nation of Islam program, too narrow for the bank; reparations and separatism are covered by colonial-reparations and ethnic-nation.

missingStatements.text: Racial integration is neither possible nor desirable.
missingStatements.rationale: Malcolm X said integration will not work and called gains tokenism.

notes: Black supremacy is a label applied by outside watchdogs and used by a few historical figures such as Leonard Howell; it is not one organised ideology. After 1975 the Nation of Islam under W. Deen Mohammed dropped the doctrine and Louis Farrakhan's revived Nation retained it. Answers on most economic and institutional questions are inferences.
